facts.statement: Neimongosaurus was a herbivorous theropod dinosaur belonging to the therizinosaurian group.
facts.quote: Neimongosaurus (meaning "Nei Mongol lizard") is a genus of herbivorous therizinosaurian theropod dinosaur that lived in China during the Late Cretaceous period.

facts.statement: The fossils were found in 1999 at a site called Sanhangobi, located 20 km southwest of Erenhot in Inner Mongolia.
facts.quote: In 1999, a team from the Ministry of Land and Resources, based in Hohhot, Inner Mongolia, was conducting field work at Sanhangobi, 20 km southwest of Erenhot.

facts.statement: The species was named Neimongosaurus yangi in 2001 by Zhang Xiaohong, Xu Xing, Paul Sereno, Kwang Xuewen, and Tan Lin.
facts.quote: In 2001, Zhang Xiaohong, Xu Xing, Paul Sereno, Kwang Xuewen and Tan Lin assigned them to a new genus and species of therizinosaurid dinosaur, Neimongosaurus yangi, designating LH V0001 as the holotype.

facts.statement: Researchers estimated the body length of Neimongosaurus to be between 2 and 3 meters.
facts.quote: Zhang et al., in 2001, estimated its body length at 2–3 m.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated the body mass of Neimongosaurus to be 350 kg.
facts.quote: In 2016, Gregory S. Paul estimated its body length at 3 m, and its body mass at 350 kg.

facts.statement: The lower jaw of Neimongosaurus had a toothless front region followed by five tooth sockets.
facts.quote: At the front of the dentary is an edentulous (toothless) region. Behind that is the alveolar margin which preserves five alveoli, or tooth sockets.

facts.statement: Only one tooth was fully erupted in the known jaw material, while a replacement tooth crown was visible in the second socket.
facts.quote: Only one, the third alveolus, contains a functioning tooth, though the second bears the crowns of a replacement tooth that had yet to fully erupt.

facts.statement: A hole for blood vessels and nerves was located approximately 15 mm behind the front of the lower jaw.
facts.quote: A neurovascular foramen, through which both blood vessels and nerves would have exited the skull, is situated about 15 mm behind the symphysis.

facts.statement: The fossil record preserves a total of seventeen vertebrae for Neimongosaurus.
facts.quote: Neimongosaurus' vertebral column is represented by a total of seventeen vertebrae.

facts.statement: Researchers tentatively suggested Neimongosaurus had fourteen neck vertebrae, giving it one of the longest necks among non-bird dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Zhang et al. suggested, tentatively that a total of fourteen were present. This would mean that Neimongosaurus would have had one of the longest cervical columns of any non-avian theropod, longer than that of taxa such as Nanshiungosaurus, which had twelve or fewer.

facts.statement: The presence of twenty-two tail vertebrae suggests Neimongosaurus had a relatively short tail.
facts.quote: Twenty-two caudal (tail) vertebrae are known, suggesting that Neimongosaurus had a fairly short tail.

facts.statement: The best-preserved upper arm bone of Neimongosaurus measured 22.2 cm in length.
facts.quote: The left humerus, the best preserved, measured 22.2 cm in length.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Neimongosaurus could extend its arms forward to reach and grasp vegetation.
facts.quote: This ability to extend their arms considerably forwards may have helped Neimongosaurus reach and grasp for foliage.

facts.statement: Fossils of Neimongosaurus come from the Iren Dabasu Formation in China.
facts.quote: Its fossils are known from the strata of the Iren Dabasu Formation.

facts.statement: Neimongosaurus lived between 85.7 and 72.2 million years ago during the Santonian to Campanian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Campanian (85.7 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Later studies placed Neimongosaurus within the family Therizinosauridae as a close relative of Segnosaurus.
facts.quote: Subsequent cladistic analyses have indicated a position in the more derived Therizinosauridae, with Clark et al. in 2004 recovering it as the sister taxon of Segnosaurus.

facts.statement: A 2019 study grouped Neimongosaurus with Erliansaurus, Suzhousaurus, and Therizinosaurus within the Therizinosauridae family.
facts.quote: However, in 2019, Scott Hartman et al. once again recovered Neimongosaurus as a therizinosaurid, forming a clade with Erliansaurus, Suzhousaurus and Therizinosaurus.

facts.statement: Neimongosaurus is classified as a member of the Therizinosauridae family.
The only known species is N. yangi, named in honor of the paleontologist Yang Zhongjian.
facts.quote: One species, N. yangi, is known, named after Chinese palaeontologist Yang Zhongjian.

rejected.statement: Two specimens of Neimongosaurus were discovered in 1999 and formally described in 2001.
rejected.quote: It is known from two specimens, discovered in 1999 by researchers from the Ministry of Land and Resources and described two years later.

rejected.statement: The forearm bone was about 80% the length of the upper arm bone and expanded at both ends.
rejected.quote: The radius measured roughly eighty percent the length of the humerus, and was expanded somewhat on both ends.

rejected.statement: The shin bone was approximately 85% as long as the upper arm bone.
rejected.quote: The tibia was approximately eighty-five percent as long as the humerus.
